themes_detail.label: Dead trees spike in Fort Greene
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 6 reports THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 380% increase—signaling either rapid tree die-off or newly visible damage in the neighborhood's park and street canopy.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.91, 380% spike)
Coincides with illegal tree damage spike: 7 complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% increase)
Construction lead dust complaints also elevated last week (6 vs. 1.0 avg), suggesting active site work may be damaging trees
reporting_angles: On-the-ground visual survey of dead trees in Fort Greene Park and major streets; interview Parks Dept on disease or pest outbreak
Investigation into whether ongoing construction projects (1,226 DOB permits filed in 90 days, including 107 new buildings) are damaging mature trees

themes_detail.label: Construction dust and tree damage wave
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged to 7 reports LAST WEEK (409% above baseline of 1.4 per week), while construction lead dust complaints hit 6 reports last week versus 1.0 weekly average—a 500% spike—suggesting aggressive site work is degrading the neighborhood's canopy and creating air quality concerns.
evidence: Illegal tree damage: 7 complaints last week vs. 1.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.62, 409% spike)
Construction lead dust: 6 complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 3.78, 500% spike)
1,226 DOB building permits filed in past 90 days (880 alterations, 107 new buildings), including active ULURP rezonings at 395 Flatbush and Columbia Heights
reporting_angles: Identify which specific construction sites are generating the most complaints; cross-reference with DOB violations and environmental audit records
Interview residents living adjacent to active construction about dust, noise, and tree damage; assess whether lead dust is triggering health concerns

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks skyrocketed to 5 reports LAST WEEK versus a near-zero baseline of 0.1 complaints per week—a 3,900% spike with z-score of 14.74—indicating a sudden and severe disturbance pattern in what should be a quiet recreational space.
evidence: Park noise complaints: 5 reports last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 14.74, 3,900% spike, highest severity rating)
Residential noise remains elevated at 1,696 complaints over 90 days (baseline pattern), but park noise is newly anomalous
No specific incident identified in available data; source of park disturbances unclear
reporting_angles: Determine what caused the sudden noise spike in Fort Greene Park—concerts, construction, gatherings, or transit work; interview Parks Dept and local precinct
Document resident impact: interviews with park users and neighbors about noise type, duration, and frequency

themes_detail.label: Police enforcement complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Real-time enforcement complaints (typically police or traffic enforcement activity) jumped to 15 complaints THREE WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 2.0 per week—a 650% spike—suggesting either aggressive policing actions or confusion around enforcement activity.
evidence: Real-time enforcement complaints: 15 reports 3 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 6.13, 650% spike)
Investigations and Discipline (IAD) complaints also spiked 1,100% 3 weeks ago (6 complaints vs. 0.5 average)
Timing suggests a potential enforcement operation or policy change; no matching media coverage identified
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYPD or DOT launched a major enforcement sweep in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights 3 weeks ago; request incident data
Interview residents about perception of police/enforcement activity; connect to broader policing trends in the district

themes_detail.label: Electrical hazards spike
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints surged to 6 reports THREE WEEKS AGO versus 0.9 per week baseline—a 586% increase—suggesting potential wiring failures, exposed hazards, or widespread outages in residential or commercial buildings.
evidence: Electrical complaints: 6 reports 3 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 6.57, 586% spike)
Heat/hot water complaints remain elevated at 1,119 over 90 days, suggesting aging building infrastructure
No follow-up data available to confirm if spike has resolved or is ongoing
reporting_angles: Request DOB and Con Edison inspection records for electrical violations in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights; identify patterns by building age or block
Assess whether electrical hazards correlate with heat/water complaints, indicating broader building system failures
